VR.1.1.1.note: Fourth review, vyākhyā only. Correct as it stands. Rule 10: the verse is narrative and is now told story-first and in order: who Vālmīki was, then the event (एकदा सः नारदं प्रश्नं परिपप्रच्छ), then the question सः नारदः कीदृशः आसीत् ? leading into the description. Only what a learner would not know is explained (स्वाध्यायः, वाग्विदां वरः, मुनिपुङ्गवः); तपस्वी and परिपप्रच्छ are no longer defined, and प्रश्नं परिपप्रच्छ makes the verb clear by itself. Rule 9: इत्युक्ते once, इति आशयः once. Rule 5: two stretching constructions, the present participle जानताम् and the finite passive उच्यते. Rule 1: connected prose. Rule 2: all boundaries clean (नारदं प्रश्नं परिपप्रच्छ, जनानां मध्ये, आसीत्, अतएव); anusvāra only before consonants. Rule 3: connectors अतएव and इति आशयः are used correctly; there is no relative clause in this verse, which I accept for a narrative verse under rule 10 (the rhetorical question does the work). Rule 4: स्वाध्यायः इत्युक्ते वेदस्य पठनम् and the explanation of वाग्विदां वरः are correct. Rule 6: only the verse's compounds. Rule 7: all eight significant padas in bold; 6 sentences; nothing added (एकदा is connective; सदा now stands with निरतः of Nārada, where it belongs). Grammar faultless, including the double accusative नारदं प्रश्नं परिपप्रच्छ.

VR.1.1.2.note: Unchanged since the third review, where it passed rules 1–7 and grammar; checked now for the two new rules. Rule 9: इत्युक्ते once (साम्प्रतम् इत्युक्ते इदानीम्); इति आशयः once, in the form इति वाल्मीकेः प्रश्नस्य आशयः; the other explanations use यः … सः, यस्य … सः and a participial phrase with इति उच्यते, so the means are varied. Rule 10: this is a verse of questions, not of events, so story order does not arise; it does not define every pada (गुणवान् and वीर्यवान् are left to the padārtha). Stretching constructions as counted before: two (स्मरन्, उच्यते).

VR.1.1.3.note: The vyākhyā is unchanged since the third review, where it was found correct on rules 1–7 and grammar; it needs no change. Rule 9: इत्युक्ते once (चारित्रम् इत्युक्ते शोभनम् आचरणम्); इति आशयः once; the rest by यः … सः, यं … सः and चेत्. Rule 10: a verse of questions; विद्वान् is rightly left undefined. Stretching constructions as counted before: two (पृच्छ्यते, दृष्ट्वा). The flag only carries forward the STANDING POINTS FOR THE SCHOLAR: (1) एकप्रियदर्शनः is read by the owner's ruling as एकः (अद्वितीयः) प्रियदर्शनः; the alternative, a bahuvrīhi एकम् (केवलम् / सदा) प्रियं दर्शनं यस्य सः, exists in the tradition and is recorded here only for completeness. (2) Linga still to be verified in the kośas (I am working from memory): चारित्र नपुं rests on Apte (चारित्रम्), I do not recall it in the Amarakośa; भूत in सर्वभूतेषु नपुं rests on Apte and on the constant usage सर्वाणि भूतानि, while the Amarakośa nānārtha line as I recall it (… भूतं प्राण्यतीते समे त्रिषु) gives the sense 'living being' without a fixed gender.

VR.1.1.4.note: Correct as it stands. The owner's two wording changes are in and are right: यः च क्रोधं जित्वा वर्तते सः जितक्रोधः (च in place of the contrast-marking तु), and the closing युद्धे क्रुद्धात् यस्मात् देवाः अपि भीताः भवन्ति, सः कः इति आशयः, where यस्मात् … सः are matched correlatives, क्रुद्धात् agrees with यस्मात् in the ablative that the ruling on कस्य requires, and the unanchored सः पुरुषः of the earlier version is gone. Rule 9: इत्युक्ते twice (आत्मवान्, संयुगः), the limit; इति आशयः once; the other words by यः … सः and यस्य … सः. Rule 5: two stretching constructions, the gerund जित्वा and the finite passive उच्यते. Rule 2: all boundaries clean (नारदम् अन्यत् अपि, क्रुद्धात् यस्मात्, युद्धम् ;). Rules 1, 3, 4, 6: as found before, all in order. Rule 7: all significant padas in bold; 6 sentences; speaker named, linked by अन्यत् अपि; nothing added (अन्तिमः प्रश्नः is true of the text). Rule 10: a verse of questions, not of events.

VR.1.1.5.note: Correct as it stands. Rule 9: इत्युक्ते once (कौतूहलम्); इति आशयः now once, at the close; the first one is replaced by the plain clause सा च तस्य महती अस्ति, which is grammatical (सा and महती agree with इच्छा; तस्य points back to Vālmīki, the सः of the same sentence) and still explains परम्. Rule 5: two stretching constructions, the gerund पृष्ट्वा and the finite passive उच्यते (पृष्टम् is a क्त form and is not counted, as in the owner's sample). Rule 2: all boundaries clean (पृष्टं तत् एव अत्र एतत् इति, कौतूहलम् अस्ति, महती अस्ति ।). Rule 3: यत् … तत्, यः … सः, अतएव, ततः. Rules 1, 4, 6: in order as before. Rule 7: all fourteen significant padas in bold; 5 sentences; speaker named, linked by एवं प्रश्नान् पृष्ट्वा; the closing inference (अतएव वाल्मीकिः नारदं पृच्छति) is the plain purpose of the line and is marked as आशयः. Rule 10: the frame is told in order (he asks, gives his reason, then turns to Nārada's ability); only एतत्, कौतूहलम् and एवंविधः नरः are explained.
